login.title: Log in
login.error: Wrong email or password, or too many attempts. Try again in a few minutes.
login.expired: The login took too long. Please start again.
login.badEmail: This does not look like an email address.

code.leadBackup: Enter one of the backup codes you saved when you set up your authenticator app. Each works once.
code.leadTotp: Enter the 6-digit code shown by your authenticator app.
code.leadPrefilled: Your code is filled in: confirm to log in.
code.leadEmail: We emailed you a 6-digit code and a link. They expire in {minutes} minutes.
code.error: This code is wrong or has expired.
code.sent: New code sent. Codes sent earlier no longer work.

account.title: Settings
account.lead: Kwazat only keeps what logging in needs: your email address, a password and a second factor, plus your language.
account.emailStep: Change confirmed. If the address below is not the new one yet, open the link we sent to the new address to finish.
account.emailSent: Check your current mailbox: we sent a link to confirm the change. A second link then goes to the new address.
account.passwordLength: The new password must have {min} to {max} characters.
account.passwordChanged: Password changed. Your other devices are logged out.
account.twoFactorEmail: Code sent by email at each login.
account.backupDone: New backup codes (the old ones no longer work). They are not shown again:
account.themeLead: Dark, light, or the same as your device.
account.languageLead: Language of the interface. By default, your browser’s.
account.tooMany: Too many attempts. Try again in {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
account.redLinesLead: What you do not want to support, checked against every sheet on your device.

twoFactor.leadChange: Choose how you confirm it is you when you log in. The method you choose replaces the current one.
twoFactor.leadSetUp: Every Kwazat account needs a second factor. Choose one to continue.
twoFactor.doneTotp: Your authenticator app is now your second factor.
twoFactor.doneEmail: Codes sent by email are now your second factor.
twoFactor.backupLead: Keep them somewhere safe (a password manager). Each one lets you log in once if you lose your phone. They are not shown again.
twoFactor.scan: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app (for example Proton Pass, Aegis, 2FAS or your password manager), then enter the 6-digit code it shows.
twoFactor.emailSent: We emailed you a 6-digit code. Enter it here to confirm this address can receive your codes.
twoFactor.emailDescription: Each login, we email you a 6-digit code and a link that fills it in.
twoFactor.totpDescription: A code from an app on your phone or in your password manager. Works offline; comes with backup codes.
twoFactor.wrongCode: This code is wrong or has expired.
twoFactor.sent: New code sent. Codes sent earlier no longer work.
twoFactor.tooMany: Too many attempts. Try again in {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.

signup.title: Create your account
signup.lead: Enter your email address and choose a password.
signup.ruleEmail: Does not contain your email address
signup.tip: Length matters more than symbols: a phrase of four or five unrelated words is easy to remember and hard to guess. A password manager is even better.

error.email: This does not look like an email address.
error.weak: This password is too weak: see the checks below.
error.exists: An account already exists for this address.
error.rate: Too many attempts. Try again in a few minutes.

backupCodes.failed: Copy failed: select the codes by hand.

redLinesSettings.title: Your red lines
redLinesSettings.lead: Choose what you do not want to support. Kwazat states the facts with their sources; you decide what counts for you.
redLinesSettings.loading: Opening your red lines on this device…
redLinesSettings.unlockFailed: Your red lines could not be opened on this device. Nothing was changed.
redLinesSettings.consentSensitive: Red lines can reveal your opinions or beliefs: they are sensitive personal data.
redLinesSettings.consentEncrypted: They are encrypted in your browser before being stored. Kwazat cannot read them, and checks them against sheets on your device only.
redLinesSettings.consentDevice: For now, the key stays on this device. If you lose it or clear this site's data, your red lines cannot be recovered: you will need to set them up again. Using them on other devices is coming soon.
redLinesSettings.consentRights: You can export or delete them at any time on this page.
redLinesSettings.consentCheckbox: I agree that Kwazat stores my red lines, encrypted, to show me which sheets match them.
redLinesSettings.lockedBody: Your red lines are encrypted with a key kept on the device where you set them up. Open this page there. Unlocking them on other devices is coming soon. You can also start over, which deletes them on every device.
redLinesSettings.ruleEntityIndirect: Links to {label}, including ownership chains and band membership
redLinesSettings.ruleProceedings: Ongoing criminal proceedings as suspect or defendant

kind.entity: Links to a person or band

kindHint.entity: Strong links (family, partner, owner, member) show in red, weaker or former ones in orange.
kindHint.conviction: Final convictions show in red; convictions under appeal or not final yet in orange.
kindHint.proceedings: Always shown in orange: people under investigation or on trial are presumed innocent.

redLinesSettings.entityNone: No known person or band with this name.
redLinesSettings.includeIndirect: Also through ownership chains and band membership
redLinesSettings.dataBody: Export your red lines as a file, or delete them on every device. Deleting also withdraws your consent.
redLinesSettings.deleteAllConfirm: Delete all your red lines on every device? This cannot be undone.
redLinesSettings.conflict: Your red lines were changed on another device. The latest version is shown: make your change again.
redLinesSettings.saveFailed: Your change could not be saved. Try again.
